- **Boundary:** Paste text: channel `send.text`, MCP `send.text`, CLI `send` stdin/`--file`
  - **What to validate:** **Rule (exact set):** multi-line text is normal (relays, plans and free-text answers are multi-line, brief §4.1 S1), so three controls are **allowed**: LF (U+000A), CR (U+000D) and TAB (U+0009). Everything else in this set is **refused**: every other C0 control (U+0000–U+0008, U+000B–U+000C, U+000E–U+001F, including ESC U+001B above all), DEL (U+007F) and every C1 control (U+0080–U+009F, including CSI U+009B). The check runs over decoded `char`s of the UTF-8 `&str`, never over raw bytes, because UTF-8 continuation bytes 0x80–0xBF are not C1 controls. This stops a bracketed-paste breakout through an embedded `ESC[201~`. **Reject, don't strip:** a text that holds a refused character is refused whole; no refused character is ever removed and the rest typed. **The typed text, an inner CR as one LF and the trailing CR and LF removed, allowed characters only:** after `validate_paste_text` has passed on the text as received, the wrapper's `send` takes the typed text once (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`: every CR LF pair as one LF, every other CR as one LF, and every trailing CR and LF removed, in any order; it holds no CR, and nothing else changes, not a TAB, a space, or an LF that is not at the very end), and from there on it is the only text `send` uses: the local-command classification (a listed local command followed by LF, CR or CRLF is that command: `/clear` and a CRLF is `/clear`), the in-flight text the delivery-confirmation exact match compares, `text_bytes` and the paste. A text that ends in CR, LF or CRLF and holds a refused character is still refused `control-character` with nothing typed.
 The LF removal is the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-07T15:21Z, every option and the `/clear`-plus-newline consequence shown to him, relayed by the overseer (chunk 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed); the CR and CRLF removal is the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-09, the options shown, relayed by the overseer (chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup); typing a CR or a CR LF inside a text as the LF the CLI submits is the founder's ruling, live in the overseer's dialog, 2026-10-09T16:51Z, the options shown, relayed by the operator (chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text). Only CR and LF, both allowed characters, are rewritten or removed: the set of accepted texts is unchanged, the typed text of a valid text is valid and holds no character that is neither in the received text nor LF (a 512-case property pins it), no refused character is typed or removed, a raw channel client gets the same rule from the wrapper, and the delivery-confirmation match stays an exact equality with no tolerance on the submitted side. **An empty typed text is refused:** a text whose typed text is empty, the empty text included, is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (`NotDelivered::EmptyText`, exit 13) on both sides: by the client (`refusal_of` in `src/cmd/send.rs`, which reads a refused character first and then the empty typed text) before any frame, with a `send-refused{side:"client"}` line, and by the wrapper's `send` directly after the typed text is taken and before the first wheel read, with nothing reserved, issued or typed (the name, the condition and the hint are the founder's ruling of 2026-10-09, relayed; the rung is the overseer's).
 **Where it runs:** `viola_core::validate_paste_text(&str) -> Result<(), NotDelivered>` (`Err(NotDelivered::ControlCharacter)`), called client-side before sending (CLI `viola send` in `src/cmd/send.rs`: exit 13 before any frame and a `send-refused{side:"client"}` line; the MCP `send` tool in `viola-mcp`, since chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers: `validate_paste_text`, then the empty-typed-text check, each refused as `{"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"control-character"|"empty-text"}` with one client-side `send-refused` line, before any frame) and again by the wrapper's `send` (`src/run/send.rs`) before anything is typed — first in its refusal order, and authoritative. The paste itself is one `ESC[200~…ESC[201~` + CR `write_all` of the typed text through `viola-pty`'s `PasteHandle`. **Wire outcome:** refusal `not-delivered` with detail `control-character`, then `not-delivered` with detail `empty-text`, both checked before the Conventions refusal order.
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-core`; `src/cmd/send.rs`; `src/run/send.rs`; `viola-pty` `PasteHandle`

- **Boundary:** Channel frames (IPC ndjson)
  - **What to validate:** **Size cap:** wrap the stream reader in `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` before `read_line`; an over-limit frame gets `-32600` and the connection is closed. **Depth:** serde_json's default recursion limit of 128 (never `unbounded_depth`). **Version:** the `v` check (`-32602`). **Closed types:** `behavior` is a closed enum (`allow`/`deny`, `approve`/`revise`), `dialog_id` is `u64`, and `link`/`unlink` `driver`/`driven` go through `ViolaName::try_new`. **`send` params (wrapper):** `text` is a string and `from` is absent, `null` or a string that passes `ViolaName::try_new`; anything else is `-32602` `"invalid params"` with `data: null`, before `validate_paste_text` runs. **`wait` / `last` params (wrapper):** `after` and `timeout_ms` are each absent or a non-negative integer that fits `u64` (`null`, a negative, a fraction or a string is `-32602` `"invalid params"` with `data: null`), `from` follows the `send` rule (one shared check), and unknown fields are ignored. The frame envelope types no method param, so a mistyped `from` reaches the method's `-32602`, never an envelope `-32600`. **`hook.dialog` params (wrapper):** `kind` is a closed dialog kind, `data` is an object, `hook_event` is closed, and `tool`, `input` and `continuation` are closed or absent; an invalid frame is not registered. **`answer` params (wrapper):** `dialog_id` is `u64`, `from` follows the `send` rule, `response` maps into the closed per-kind enums, then `validate_paste_text` runs on its free text. **`pause` / `release` params (wrapper):** `pause`'s `from` follows the `send` rule; `release`'s `budget` is absent or a bool (anything else, `null` included, is `-32602` `"invalid params"` with `data: null`), and its `from` is absent or `null` — a string `from` is `-32602` `"invalid params"` with `data: {"reason":"release-from-driver"}`, any other type `-32602` with `data: null`.
 **`link` / `unlink` params (wrapper):** `driver` and `driven` are strings that pass `ViolaName::try_new` (one shared check); a missing, non-string or invalid name, a `driven` other than the serving wrapper's own name and a `driver` equal to `driven` are each `-32602` `"invalid params"` with `data: null`, no line written; neither method reads `from`, so a `from` of any shape changes nothing.
 **`hook.event` re-validation (wrapper):** `kind` is one of the five hook kinds, `data` is an object, and for `prompt-submitted` `text` is a string and `origin` is `harness` · `human`; an invalid event is not appended.
 **A reply, read by a client:** `reply_of` (`src/cmd/client.rs`) and `of_reply` (`crates/viola-mcp/src/result.rs`) take a `refusal` or a string `detail` only as a code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`), and a fault only through `viola_channel::sanitised_fault` (§ Error Handling). **The refusals on the log:** the three `-32602` faults read `channel-response`'s `detail` `unsupported-version`, `invalid-params` and `release-from-driver`, on the server's and the client's line, level WARN, no param name or value on it; every other `channel-response` line has no `detail`.
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-channel` framing; serde 1.0.229; serde_json 1.0.151; nutype 0.8.0

- **Boundary:** Hook stdin (all hook events + `hook statusline`)
  - **What to validate:** **Size cap:** `Read::take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` on `read_to_end`, so an over-limit payload is detected, never silently truncated; over the limit, fail open (exit 0, no body, `hook-decision` detail `oversize-stdin` + `parse-rejected{parser:"hook-stdin", detail:"oversize"}` in `diagnostics/`). **Event argument:** the word `statusline` (with no `--capture`) is taken first and is not a `HookEvent`; any other `<event>` maps into the closed `HookEvent` (9 events: the seven spine and async events plus the dialog tier, `PreToolUse` and `PermissionRequest`); an unknown event, a clap error or an absent/invalid `VIOLA_NAME` exits 0 with nothing written anywhere. The event and dialog paths then canonicalise the instance directory and run the instance check (`canonical`, then `trusted`, in `src/cmd/hook.rs`: `viola_state::strict::check_instance`) before the diagnostics level and obs init: a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory, or an instance the check refuses, exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append. **One object:** a payload that is not one JSON object fails open with `malformed-json`. **Parsing:** tolerant (Established Decisions: Validation), but fields that decide security (dialog kind and the decision body) map into closed enums in `viola-agent-claude`: on the dialog path `viola_agent_claude::dialog::classify` maps the one object into `DialogKind` / `DialogTool`, a malformed dialog payload fails open (`AgentError::DialogMalformed`: exit 0, no body), the reply read is bounded at `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s: the ceiling, the wrapper replying `null` at its own configured hold's end), and stdout takes one write. **Question and Stop data:** each question's `option_details` takes an option's `description` and `preview` only as strings, else `null`, and never refuses the dialog (`options` keeps its labels); the Stop's `background_tasks` is read as an array of `serde::de::IgnoredAny` and carried only as its length, no element read, `null` when absent, `null` or not an array (a non-array also writes the drift entry `{"path":"background_tasks","expected":"array"}`).
 The option text crossing into `events.ndjson`, `hook.dialog`, CLI `wait --json` and the MCP `wait` is a boundary widening the founder answered himself (P4 fork Q4 of chunk 2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola, relayed by the overseer), and `background_tasks` is a count only by the same answer. **Statusline payload (`hook statusline`):** the same cap and the same one-object rule, each ending in exit 0, empty stderr, nothing printed and no `budget.json`. `viola_agent_claude::statusline::reading` is tolerant on every field: no `rate_limits` object is no reading and no write; a window that is absent or not an object is the word `"unknown"`; `used_percentage` is kept only from 0 to 100, else `"unknown"`; `resets_at` is epoch seconds or RFC 3339, written as RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds, and a malformed value becomes `"unknown"`. `budget.json` is written only by this arm. **Capture arm (hidden, `hook <event> --capture <DIR> [--answers <DIR>]`, called only by `viola verify`'s probe plugins):** `<DIR>` must be absolute and exist; stdin is read through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and written raw (verify parses it later) to an exclusively claimed `<DIR>/<PascalEvent>.<k>.json`: `viola_state::fs::create_private_new` creates it new at 0600 from `free_k`'s first free `k`, the next `k` on `AlreadyExists`, then `replace_private` writes over its own claim, so two concurrent captures never share a name. `--answers <DIR>` is read only with `--capture` (inert without it): for a dialog event (PreToolUse / PermissionRequest), the event's ordinal `j` in claim order selects `<DIR>/<Event>.<j>`, read through `take(64)` and matched exactly against the closed `ProbeAnswer` ids; `ledger::probe_body` shape-checks the filed payload (`None` on a miss) and builds the body only through `dialog::decision_body`; stdout takes one write.
 It reads no `VIOLA_*`, does no obs init and opens no channel; any failure prints and writes nothing; stderr is always empty and the exit always 0. A boundary widening ratified live by the founder at 2026-09-28 20:24:32 (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, capture arm); the `--answers` body is the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05 (M7 = A, the hook answers, never a key), relayed by the overseer. **Statusline capture arm (hidden, `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]`, called only by Run B's probe settings):** taken before the statusline pass-through; `<DIR>` must be absolute and exist; stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, refused past `MAX_FRAME`; the payload is written raw at the first free `StatusLine.<k>.json` through the same `create_private_new` claim and `replace_private` 0600 write, and `StatusLine.<k>.shell` holds exactly `bin-sh` when the `--shell` word equals `/bin/sh` byte for byte, else `other` (a missing word is `other`, the closed `ShellVerdict`); the word itself is written nowhere. It prints nothing, exits 0 on every path, reads no `VIOLA_*`, does no obs init and opens no channel, `budget.json` or snapshot; `--shell` on any other arm changes nothing, and `hook statusline` without `--capture` is unchanged. `viola verify` reads the files back through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` (the shell file capped at 16 bytes) into `ShellVerdict`. The founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows («Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`).
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-agent-claude` hook parser, `statusline::reading` and `ledger::probe_body`; root `src/cmd/hook.rs` `capture` / `free_k` / `file_from` and `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`; `viola_state::fs::create_private_new`; serde_path_to_error 0.1.20; chrono 0.4.45

- **Boundary:** MCP tool inputs (`target`, `text`, `dialog_id`, `response`, `after`, `timeout_ms`)
  - **What to validate:** The schemars 1.2.2 schemas are advisory only, because rmcp does not enforce them server-side. Deserialise `target` into `ViolaName`, `dialog_id` into `u64` and `response` into the closed channel enums, and apply `validate_paste_text` to `text` and the free-text answer fields. As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), each handler takes the raw argument object, never rmcp's typed deserialisation (a serde failure would carry serde text): `target` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `text` a string, `after` / `timeout_ms` absent, `null` or a `u64` (`wait`'s `timeout_ms` clamped to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, also its default), `dialog_id` a `u64`, `response` an object through `Response::parse`, then `validate_paste_text` on `send`'s text and on every free-text answer value. A failure is `isError: true` with `structuredContent` `{"error":"invalid-params","detail":"<field>"}` (the closed field words `target` · `text` · `after` · `timeout_ms` · `dialog_id` · `response`), text `refused: invalid-params`, and no frame; an unknown tool name is JSON-RPC `-32602`.
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-mcp` tool handlers; schemars 1.2.2; rmcp 3.4.1

- **Boundary:** MCP stdin (`viola mcp`'s transport, the driver's JSON-RPC lines)
  - **What to validate:** **Line cap:** each line passes through `viola_mcp::stdin::CappedLines` at `MAX_FRAME`, its `\n` counted, before rmcp reads it; a line of exactly the cap passes whole; a longer line releases no byte and is refused whole, never truncated and never skipped, and the reader then reads as end of stream, so the session ends as a stdin close does; at the inner end a held unterminated line within the cap is released.
 **On the cut:** after the session ends, `serve` writes one WARN `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` through `obs_event!`, holding no byte of the line, and returns what the session gave: exit 0 for an initialized session; when the cut lands before `initialize` completes, `serve` returns `ServeError::Initialize` and the `viola mcp` process exits 1, both streams empty, with that one line (`src/main.rs` `exit_code`, `Role::Mcp` + `Failed`), 11 being only the unit child's own code (`serve_child_entry`).
 **Why the reader, not the codec:** rmcp 3.4.1's stdio transport reads each line with an unbounded `read_until`, and `JsonRpcMessageCodec::new_with_max_length` bounds only the writer, so the bound on rmcp's input sits on the reader viola hands it, never on the codec.
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-mcp` `stdin::CappedLines` (crate-private), handed to rmcp 3.4.1 as `(CappedLines::new(stdin, MAX_FRAME), stdout)` through the `(reader, writer)` transport `transport-io` already enables, no rmcp feature added; `viola_mcp::serve`

- **Boundary:** CLI arguments / stdin
  - **What to validate:** **Names:** every `ViolaName` argument uses `#[arg(value_parser = parse_viola_name)]`, which calls `ViolaName::try_new`. **Home path:** `--home` and `VIOLA_DIR` are canonicalised (`std::fs::canonicalize`, once the home exists; the plain drive form on Windows — the resolution as landed is **Home resolution** below) and then pass the `~/.viola/` strict-modes check before any snapshot, `statusline_command` or ledger read. `viola hook <event>` on its nine `HookEvent` arms and `hook statusline`, each outside `--capture`, canonicalise the instance directory and run `viola_state::strict::check_instance` (`canonical` and `trusted`, shared in `src/cmd/hook.rs`) before the diagnostics level, obs init and any stdin, `budget.json`, snapshot or `statusline_command` use; on its event path it requires an absolute `VIOLA_DIR` ending `<home>/instances/<name>` and a `VIOLA_NAME` that passes `ViolaName::try_new`, and a malformed, absent or refused instance is a silent no-op (exit 0, nothing written); its hidden `--capture <DIR>` arm (and `hook statusline --capture <DIR>`, whose hidden `--shell <WORD>` maps only into the closed `ShellVerdict`) reads no `VIOLA_*` and requires an absolute, existing `<DIR>` instead, and its hidden `--answers <DIR>` is read only with `--capture`, each answer file through `take(64)` into the closed `ProbeAnswer` id (Hook stdin row). `viola verify` runs `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log (a refusal is the home pair, exit 1, no step line), and its `update_stamps` refuses before it creates `ledger/` or reads the stamps (Own state files row); `viola run`'s version gate reads it through `read_stamps_strict`. **`answer` response:** the JSON from stdin or `--file` is read with `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` into the closed `response` enums.
 **`send` text:** from stdin or `--file` only, read with `Read::take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`; over the cap or not UTF-8 is exit 2 with one fixed line, a second positional argument is a clap usage error, and the text then passes `validate_paste_text` and the empty-typed-text check (`refusal_of`: `not-delivered` / `control-character`, then `not-delivered` / `empty-text`; exit 13), both before any frame. **Frame verbs:** `viola send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` each run `client::refuse_untrusted` first: `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`; a refusal is exit 21 with the instance pair, or under `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, with nothing opened under the home and no line. A passed check is followed by the liveness pre-check `live_endpoint` (the endpoint, `pid` and `started_at`) and then, on Linux and Windows, the server check before the frame (IPC client-side server verification row). `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools run `check_instance` before `live_endpoint`; a refusal returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail: null`, no frame and no line. **`wait` / `last` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new` (the verbs share `send`'s name parser), and `--after` / `--timeout-ms` are clap `u64` (a non-integer is a usage error, exit 2). **`answer` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `<dialog_id>` a clap `u64`.
 **`pause` / `release` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new`; their `from` comes from `VIOLA_NAME` only. **`revive` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new` (the verbs' shared name parser); `--id <ID>` through a clap value parser that accepts only the session-id shape (anything else is a usage error, exit 2); `--list` conflicts with `--id`, `--fork` and the trailing arguments; the words after `--` go to the child as argv elements of a direct spawn; `--json` is accepted on both arms (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal then prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` on stdout (stderr empty, exit 1), `<code>` one of the closed `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` (through `client::refused_document`), and `--list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[{"ts","cause","id"},…]}}` in log order (the escaped `ts`, the closed cause word, the session-shaped id) — codes, closed words and session-shaped ids only, never a path or pid; a refusal `run`'s start makes after a passed preflight prints no document (owed to the route entry "Exit-cause code catalogue"); `--list` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` logs `process-start` / `process-exit` in the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson` only after its strict-modes check passed. Both arms run the strict-modes check on the instance's files before any snapshot or log value is used, and the start arm also runs `check_home_tree` (through `run`'s `checked_exe`) before its wrapper log: a refusal is exit 1 with the home or the instance pair, no log and no child (under `--json`, `strict-modes-failed`). **`list` arguments:** `[--json]` only, no name.
 **`link` / `unlink` arguments:** `<driver>` and `<driven>` through `ViolaName::try_new` (the verbs' shared name parser), and `--json`; the verbs' instance is the driven one, `instances/<driven>` joined only from that parsed name and checked by `check_instance` before any snapshot read, through `client::refuse_untrusted`, the one check they share with the six frame verbs. A `driver` equal to `driven` is not refused client-side: the wrapper refuses it (`-32602`, the Channel frames row).
 **Home resolution:** every CLI verb (`run` and `revive` included; `hook` keeps its own shape check), and the hidden `viola mcp` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), resolves the home through `resolved_home` (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): `--home` as given; else the `instance_of` home when `VIOLA_NAME` passes `ViolaName::try_new` and `VIOLA_DIR` is an absolute `<home>/instances/<name>` (a pair that fails the check falls through, never refuses); else `<user home>/.viola`; then `canonical_home` applies `std::fs::canonicalize` when the path exists (on Windows a `\\?\C:\…` result is written back as `C:\…`, only the verbatim-drive prefix stripped; `\\?\UNC\…`, `\\?\Volume{…}\…` and `\\.\…` stay as given), while a path that does not exist keeps `std::path::absolute`'s spelling and nothing is created. The CLI verbs' `VIOLA_DIR` step and the canonicalisation, `mcp`'s use of them included, widen what chooses a CLI verb's home: a widening the founder ratified (his own word, relayed verbatim by the operator, 2026-10-19). `viola list`'s `board::scan` then runs `check_path` on the home and on `instances/` (each through `symlink_metadata`, a link never followed) and `check_instance` per instance before any file under the home is opened (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list).
  - **How (stack-specific):** `src/main.rs` clap 4.6.7 derive; `viola-state` home resolution

- **Boundary:** Configuration values (`config.json`)
  - **What to validate:** Tolerant parse (unknown keys counted). The budget thresholds are the two top-level keys `five_hour` and `seven_day` (defaults 90 and 85), read once at the wrapper's start, and by `viola list` at each run, both through `run::budget::read_thresholds` under the same rule (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; each rejection is logged through `obs::log_config_rejection`, under a `VIOLA_NAME` only, and a refused `list` reads no `config.json`): a value must be a JSON whole number that fits `Percent` (0–100, `Percent::try_new`), else that key alone takes its default and is reported as one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"malformed"}` line per bad key; a document that is no object, or whose `v` is not 1, gives both defaults and no rejection from this read; no value of either key switches the gate off. The dialog hold is the top-level key `dialog_hold_s`, read once at the wrapper's start through `run::dialog::read_hold` right after the thresholds: a JSON whole number of seconds that fits `DialogHold` (60–3600, `DialogHold::try_new`; default 60, `DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT`), else the hold takes 60 and is reported as one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"malformed"}` line; a document that is no object, or whose `v` is not 1, gives 60 and no rejection from this read; no value makes the hold zero or unbounded, and no env var or flag sets it (a boundary widening the founder answered himself, chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver, `inputs#I2` Q1). `port` goes into `u16`. `diagnostics_level` is the closed set `info` \| `debug`; any other value falls back to `info` and is reported as `parse-rejected`. `claude_env_keep` (the Unix R8 pass-list) is an array of at most 32 names, each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`; a bad value is rejected WHOLE (never partly accepted) and reported as `parse-rejected`, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect (not an error). `v` is checked, and the read is capped at `MAX_FRAME`.
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-state` (the `diagnostics_level` read lives in the root bin `viola::obs`, the `claude_env_keep` read in the root bin `src/run/env.rs`, the threshold read in the root bin `src/run/budget.rs`, the hold read in the root bin `src/run/dialog.rs`, each its own `take(MAX_FRAME)` read; `Percent` and `DialogHold` are `viola-core`'s); nutype 0.8.0

- **Files (`~/.viola/`):** Plaintext by design (Established Decisions: Database / State Store). Protected by OS permissions only:
  - Unix: 0700 directories and 0600 files, except the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola`, which is 0700.
  - Windows: the inherited `%USERPROFILE%` DACL (user + SYSTEM + Administrators), or an explicit protected user + SYSTEM DACL for a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%`.
  - The protected owner-only DACL of a home viola makes outside `%USERPROFILE%` reads `D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)`, canonical SDDL spelling the runner's user (the local Administrator, RID 500) `LA` (as measured on `windows-2025` at viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity/report.md).
  - The strict-modes check runs at startup (Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control). On Windows a plain home made before viola (`create_dir_all`) is refused `Writable`, the refused entry an inherited allow ACE that grants a write right to a SID the check does not trust (read by the right, whichever SID holds it), so such a home is one the check refuses (as measured on `windows-2025` at viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds/report.md).
  - **Code-bearing artefacts:**
    - `viola run` always rewrites `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` files with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (`replace_private_shared`: a replace that fails counts as done only when the file already holds exactly the rendered bytes, which a concurrent start of the same version writes) rather than trusting an existing copy.
    - `instances/<name>/settings.json` (the per-session override whose statusline command Claude Code executes) is `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":"<pinned path> hook statusline"}}`. `viola run` rewrites it whole at every start, a revived start included, with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (`viola_state::fs::replace_private`, 0600), after the first snapshot and before the spawn, and never reuses an existing copy. Its command uses the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` path (§ Universal). It is written only on Unix, and only when every character of the pinned path is an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `_ - . / :` (`viola_agent_claude::statusline::override_document`), since a shell runs the string unquoted; for any other path, and on Windows, no override is written. The Windows half is cut by his word the same day and owed to the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements".
    - `<hash>` is a truncated SHA-256 of the exe bytes (the first 16 hex characters of the digest). Before reusing an existing `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)`, `viola run` re-hashes the file with SHA-256 and compares the truncated result with `<hash>`. On a mismatch it refuses to start (exit 1). A non-cryptographic fallback is banned (§ Data Protection). Because the hash is cryptographic, this catches substitution as well as accidental corruption. A lost placement whose copy is reused reads `ok` on `run.pin_copy` (`ok|pinned-hash-mismatch`).

subject: data-rest
text: - **Code-bearing artefacts (one tree's release builds):** Clean release builds of one tree can give two files whose loaded sections are equal, so one tree can key two `bin/<key>/` and `plugin/<key>/` folders; the reading stands at architecture §Established Decisions [Deployment / Distribution], no cause is claimed, and acting on it is the founder's.

subject: data-rest
text: - **Logs (the wrapper's process log) and the link verbs' output:** the wrapper's `link` / `unlink` methods open no span and write no process-log line of their own; its `channel-request` / `channel-response` pair carries `method:"link"|"unlink"` and no name, so no driver name reaches the wrapper's process log. `viola link` / `viola unlink` print only their own parsed `ViolaName` arguments, never a name read back from the reply or the log.

subject: data-rest
text: - **Logs (the diagnostics opens):** `open_role_file` and `write_detail` run `viola_state::strict::check_diagnostics` on the existing `diagnostics/` folder and on the role or detail file before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything: a symlink is refused; a folder takes the read rule; a file takes the read rule on Unix and the write rule on Windows; an absent path passes. A refusal is a failed open: the writer ends at `std::io::sink` and the detail line is dropped.

Every ban, the tree form included (probe `channel-tokio-edge` and its channel control; `14/14 banned, control clean`, counted as the `probes=(` rows of `scripts/deny-probes.sh` plus the planted channel probe, as measured at viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary/report.md), is proven live by `scripts/deny-probes.sh`.

subject: bootstrap
text:
- **auth-scaffolding-baseline:** Narrowed to the local boundary; no auth library. Each arch amendment (Decisions Log) must be folded in before the first chunk that implements it:
  - Amendments 3 (`control-character` detail) and 6 (`MAX_FRAME`): before the `viola-core` chunk. Its `control-character` detail lands with the route's "Confirmed send" entry.
  - Amendment 2 (Unix endpoint move): folded into architecture §Occupied Resources (IPC endpoints) by the `viola-channel` chunk ("Wrapper channel").
  - Amendment 4 (`release-from-driver`): landed in the `viola` bin channel dispatch with chunk 2026-10-04-the-wheel (`viola_channel::ProtocolError::ReleaseFromDriver`, −32602).
  - Amendment 7 (largest-hook-payload ledger row): before the `viola verify` chunk.
  - Amendment 8 (SHA-256 `<hash>`): before the chunk that writes `bin/`.
  - `viola-channel`: per-OS listener hardening (Windows SDDL converted by windows-sys into interprocess `security_descriptor` + windows-sys SID lookup; Unix 0700 per-user socket directory + chmod 0600 after the bind + `peer_creds` euid check). The SDDL, the per-user directory and the 0600 socket landed with "Wrapper channel", ahead of Epoch 6's admission entry; the `peer_creds` decision and the directory verification stay with their route entries.
  - `viola-channel` client: the SQOS open (windows-sys `CreateFileW` + `Stream::try_from(OwnedHandle)`) and the peer pid (`Client::server_pid`, `TokioClient::server_pid`, interprocess `peer_creds().pid()`); the verdict, pid + sysinfo start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at`, lives in `viola-state` liveness (`verify_server`, `ServerVerdict`), called by the root bin and `viola-mcp`, built on Linux and Windows; every client reads the snapshot only after the instance's strict-modes check (`viola_state::strict::check_instance`; the six CLI frame verbs and `link` / `unlink` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, the hook event and dialog paths through `trusted`, `viola mcp`'s frame tools directly; a refusal writes no line), then makes the liveness pre-check and the server check. The SQOS spike passed (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`); the client reuses the recipe `tests/channel_sqos_open.rs` pins.
  - `viola-state`: home 0700/0600 creation (the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` is the only 0700 file) and the strict-modes check (`viola_state::strict`), including the trusted files; the read rule (Unix `mode & 0o077`; Windows no `READ_RIGHTS` grant to another SID) on the home, `instances/<name>/` and its `diagnostics/`; `check_home_tree` (the home tree at `run` and `revive` start and in `verify`); `check_diagnostics` (the diagnostics opens); `check_present` (the `conpty/` companions); and the `Readable` and `Symlink` refusals; on Windows, the protected user + SYSTEM DACL for a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` and the owner + DACL check (windows-sys).
  - `viola-state`: SHA-256 re-hash of `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` before reuse. The hash crate is `sha2 =0.11.0` (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`).
  - `viola run` / `viola-state`: rewrite `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` files and `instances/<name>/settings.json` with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (0600, mode set on the temp file before the write) at every start, never reusing an existing copy. The `settings.json` override is rewritten on Unix when the pinned path passes the plain-character rule; it is not written on Windows or for a pinned path a shell could misread (§ Data Protection, Code-bearing artefacts). Every exec-form `command` they carry is the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` path, never a PATH lookup (§ Universal). `ledger/stamps.json` is written only by `viola verify`, under its `.lock`, with 0600.

text:
- **secret-scanning-ci-gate:** No repo secret scanner in v1. There are no secrets in the repo or CI, and no scanner was researched (see the Decisions Log). The CI `test` job does run obs-plan §9's artifact canary scan: `viola-harness secret-scan` over test-home diagnostics, the harness capture except `run --mutants`' `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`, and the nextest JUnit report, checked against this plan's NEVER-log floor. That one file is repository source text by construction (it trips the scan's own needles whenever it touches the scan's source), so it is skipped by exact path and the `harness-<os>` upload drops it (`!target/agent-run/chunk.diff`): it is never scanned and never uploaded, and a `chunk.diff` anywhere else under the capture is still scanned. It never prints or writes the matched bytes, and every scan-gated upload (`diag-`, `junit-`, `harness-<os>`) waits for it to pass. The `mutants.out/` upload is removed: `outcomes.json` held absolute argv paths and `log/` held test output. One upload leaves CI unscanned, admissible by content (operator ratification 2026-09-24; the second, the mutants legs' `mutants-verdict-<os>.json`, left with the CI mutation jobs on 2026-09-28, Decisions Log):
  - the nightly `fuzz` job's `fuzz/artifacts/` on failure: crash inputs the fuzzer mutated from the committed synthetic corpus. A non-synthetic corpus seed must first drop that upload. `.gitignore` excludes any local `--home` test directories so recorded state never lands in git.
